title: Roadmap handoff contracts and sprint-pulse orchestrator
creator: Marcus Li
description: Problem: Roadmap signals (timelines, blockers, API/infra assumptions) frequently fail to propagate between Eng, Design, Security, and Infra teams, causing late rework and missed cutovers. Goal: Create a lightweight handoff contract and an automated sprint-pulse orchestrator that (1) codifies minimal acceptance criteria for handoffs, (2) surfaces drifting commitments in the Roadmap Console, and (3) auto-creates stakeholder actions when a contract is at risk. This ticket scopes the initial implementation: schema for handoff contract, producer/consumer roles, UI exposure in Console as a 'handoff card', webhook/Slack alerts for pulse regressions, and a small pilot with Runtime and Console squads.
acceptance_criteria: Handoff contract schema defined (fields: owner, consumer teams, assumptions, release_window, required artifacts, acceptance_signoff)
Console shows handoff cards on initiative pages with current pulse score
Pulse rule engine runs nightly and flags contracts that move from green->amber or amber->red
When pulse becomes red, the system auto-creates a triage ticket in the consumer team's Linear queue and pings the configured Slack channel
Pilot executed with Runtime (ENG-RT) and Console (ENG-C) squads for two sprints with documented outcomes
milestones: 2026-01-25: Minimal Console UI mock and product signoff
2026-02-05: Backend rules engine prototype + webhook contract
2026-02-12: Pilot start with Runtime & Console squads
decisions: Keep handoff contract intentionally small to reduce friction: 6 required fields
Use existing Roadmap Console auth and display surface to avoid new UX primitives
Pulse scoring will combine three signals: owner heartbeat (manual), JIRA/PR status parity, and infra capacity signal (from infra telemetry)
Initial auto-ticketing will create triage tasks assigned to the consumer team rotation inbox rather than to named individuals
open_questions: What is the canonical source for infra capacity signal for private deployments? (Infra/Platform to confirm)
Should design acceptance be a formal checkbox or captured as an artifact link?
Are security signoffs required for every handoff or only for releases touching secret/PII paths?
What SLA should auto-created triage tickets carry?
